discrepancy.note: Troki shows Matthew's citation of 'Jeremy the prophet' is actually drawn from Zechariah, calling it a misapplication of the passage's real sense.

quotes.text: Here, again, we meet with the usual misapplication of Scriptural passages. The quotation, taken from Zechariah xi. 12, 13, runs as follows … The unbiassed reader need merely refer to the context, from which this passage is extracted, in order to obtain the conviction that the prophet wished to convey a far different idea than Matthew found in it.
quotes.attr: Isaac ben Abraham Troki (d. 1594), Faith Strengthened (Chizzuk Emunah) (1851), ch. XXV, on Zechariah 11:12 and Matthew 27:9.

sides.snippet: they weighed for my wages thirty pieces of silver.
sides.verseText: I said to them, \"If you think it best, give me my wages; and if not, keep them.\" So they weighed for my wages thirty pieces of silver.
